Build your future with German engineering technology. Explore GMI’s programmes and check which ones you can apply for.

German-Malaysian Institute (GMI) in Kajang, Selangor, is the outcome of a joint venture between the Governments of Malaysia and Germany. It offers a broad-based engineering education that balances practical and theoretical training, with opportunities for specialisation and self-directed learning.
Enter your SPM, O-Level/IGCSE or UEC grades and see every programme you may qualify for.
GMI’s background, official contact details, enquiries and location map.
Content adapted from the official GMI website (gmi.edu.my) and the GMI Programme Guide (May 2026). Details can change, so always confirm with GMI before applying.

GMI offers 2 pre-university programmes and 15 diplomas in 5 groups. Diplomas in the same group share the same entry requirements. Tap a programme to see its details, entry requirements and official sources.
Not stated in the sources used.

All diploma programmes
• SVM: C in Bahasa Melayu (BM 1104), a pass in Sejarah (1251), 3 vocational credits, academic CGPA 2.00, vocational CGPA 2.67, and competent in all vocational modules
• International students: TOEFL 500 or IELTS 5.0 (or equivalent)
• APEL.A T-4: accepted, with experience as determined by GMI
• Other recognised equivalent qualifications are accepted
Two diplomas from GMI’s Mechanical Engineering Department that share the same entry requirements (MQA Standard: Engineering and Engineering Technology).

This group has two diplomas from GMI’s Mechanical Engineering Department: Precision Tooling Engineering Technology and Innovative Product Design Engineering Technology. Both follow the MQA Standard for Engineering and Engineering Technology, so they have the same entry requirements.\n\nGMI’s diplomas follow its TVET learning approach of 70% practical and 30% theory, with exposure to 22 Advanced Technology Centres and internship and job placement opportunities with industry partners.
Diploma qualification (MQA Standard: Engineering and Engineering Technology)
SPM: credit in Mathematics, 1 Science/Technical/Vocational subject and 1 other subject. O-Level: Grade C in the same 3 subjects. UEC: Grade B in 3 subjects. Every route also needs a pass in English.
Mechanical Engineering Department\n• Diploma in Precision Tooling Engineering Technology\n• Diploma in Innovative Product Design Engineering Technology

MQA Standard: Engineering and Engineering Technology
Both diplomas in this group have the same minimum requirements:
• SPM: a credit in Mathematics + 1 Science/Technical/Vocational subject + 1 other subject AND a pass in English
• O-Level: Grade C in 3 subjects (same pattern) AND a pass in English
• UEC: Grade B in 3 subjects (same pattern; the other subject can be from any field) AND a pass in English
• Certificate (related field): CGPA 2.00
• Technical/Vocational or Skills Certificate (SKM Level 3): SPM with 1 credit, plus 1 year of work experience or at least 1 semester of bridging
• STPM: 1 principal in any subject, plus a pass in Mathematics, English and 1 other subject at SPM
• Pre-Diploma / Matriculation (related field): CGPA 2.00, plus SPM with 3 credits including Bahasa Melayu and 2 other subjects, AND a pass in English

Other requirements
No physical disability that would hinder practical work, no colour blindness, and a pass in a medical examination and urine test.

8 mechanical and electrical engineering technology diplomas
Eight diplomas from GMI’s Mechanical Engineering and Electrical Engineering departments that share the same entry requirements (BEM Standard, ETAC).

This group has eight engineering technology diplomas: three from GMI’s Mechanical Engineering Department and five from the Electrical Engineering Department. All of them follow the BEM Standard (ETAC), so they have the same entry requirements.\n\nGMI’s diplomas follow its TVET learning approach of 70% practical and 30% theory, with exposure to 22 Advanced Technology Centres and internship and job placement opportunities with industry partners.
Diploma qualification (BEM Standard, ETAC). Programme briefs list careers such as CNC programmer, CAD designer, production executive and assistant engineer (CNC Precision example).

Cambridge A-Level and German language pathway to study in Germany
A pre-university programme launched at GMI in 2001 for students who want to study engineering at a University of Applied Sciences in Germany.

German Universities of Applied Sciences require A-Levels, TestDaF and a Vorpraktikum (pre-study internship) for enrolment. GAPP prepares students for all three: a 20-month preparatory programme at GMI, followed by 6 months of intensive German language training at language centres in Germany. After completing both, students apply to a University of Applied Sciences (UAS) or Hochschule in Germany.
20 months at GMI + 6 months of German language training in Germany
Engineering studies at a University of Applied Sciences (UAS) / Hochschule in Germany

YTP MARA (sponsored): SPM with 8As, including English, Add Maths, Physics and Chemistry. Self-sponsored: C in English, Mathematics, Add Maths, Physics and Chemistry, plus Bahasa Melayu (SPM) or 1 other subject (IGCSE/O-Level).

Cambridge GCE A-Level
• Mathematics (9709)
• Physics (9702)
• Chemistry (9701)
• German (8027)

Also included
• German language from Level A2 to C1
• 440 hours of Vorpraktikum (pre-study technical internship)
• In Germany: German from B2 to TestDaF, an intercultural and study skills workshop, technical German, study placement advice and an internship (depends on placement)

Sponsored candidate (YTP MARA)
• Bumiputera
• SPM with “A” in English, Additional Mathematics, Physics, Chemistry and 4 other subjects (8As)

• SPM: “C” in Bahasa Melayu, English, Mathematics, Additional Mathematics, Physics and Chemistry

One-year Foundation in Engineering and Science with Universiti Teknologi PETRONAS
A strategic partnership between GMI and Universiti Teknologi PETRONAS (UTP), based on UTP’s foundation syllabus.

Foundation in Collaboration with Universiti Teknologi PETRONAS, also known as the GMI–UTP Foundation Programme (GUFP), is a one-year foundation programme based on UTP’s foundation syllabus. On completion, students are qualified to start their undergraduate programme at UTP, subject to meeting UTP’s academic requirements. English is the medium of instruction, and weekly German language classes and activities are available.
Undergraduate degree programmes at Universiti Teknologi PETRONAS (UTP)
SPM: at least C in Bahasa Melayu, English, Mathematics, Add Maths, Physics and Chemistry. IGCSE/O-Level: C in 5 subjects, including Mathematics, Physics, Chemistry and Add Maths.

Foundation in Engineering and Science
• Mathematics, Physics and Chemistry (I and II)
• Structured Algorithms and Programming
• Technical English
• Thinking Skills
• Islamic Studies / Moral Studies
• Co-curriculum
• Introduction to German culture and basic German

UTP degree pathways (May 2026 guide)
Chemical, Civil, Electrical & Electronics, Integrated, Mechanical, Petroleum, Computer and Material Engineering; BSc in Applied Physics, Industrial Physics, Applied Chemistry and Petroleum Geoscience

SPM
• Pass SPM with minimum Grade C in Bahasa Melayu, Mathematics, English, Additional Mathematics, Physics and Chemistry

IGCSE / O-Level
• Pass IGCSE/O-Level with minimum credits (Grade C) or 60% and above in 5 subjects, inclusive of Mathematics, Physics, Chemistry, Additional Mathematics and any other 1 subject

German-Malaysian Institute (GMI) is a hub for advanced skills training and the outcome of a joint venture between the Governments of Malaysia and Germany. It was set up as a company limited by guarantee. Its founders are Majlis Amanah Rakyat (MARA) and the Malaysian German Chamber of Commerce and Industry (MGCC), and its implementing agencies are MARA and Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit (GIZ) GmbH.\n\nGMI enrolled its first students in 1992 and has been at its industrial-based campus in Kajang, Selangor, since 2008. It offers full-time diploma programmes, a pre-university programme (A-Level), a foundation programme, skills upgrading courses, train-the-trainer programmes, and industrial consultancy and services.
To be an internationally competitive higher learning institution delivering advanced technical education, training and services; empowering a skilled workforce to reach its fullest potential.

To provide cutting-edge industrial solutions in advanced technical education and training through innovative blended methodologies, fostering lifelong learning and responsive to global industry demands.
